ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES — TERMLY EXAM #9
====

GRADE: PP2
SUBJECT: ENVIRONMENTAL ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only carbon dioxide
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Only water vapour

2. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

3. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying People found at home? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about People found at home.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on People found at home.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to People found at home.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for People found at home.

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT be able to;? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT be able to;.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT be able to;.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT be able to;.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Interpersonal ENVIRONMENT be able to;.

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Care for PRACTICES be able to;? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Care for PRACTICES be able to;.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Care for PRACTICES be able to;.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Care for PRACTICES be able to;.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Care for PRACTICES be able to;.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Toileting PRACTICES? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Toileting PRACTICES.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Toileting PRACTICES.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Toileting PRACTICES.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Toileting PRACTICES.

8. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 37 °C
   B. 100 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 50 °C

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Food/ PRACTICES? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Food/ PRACTICES.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Food/ PRACTICES.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Food/ PRACTICES.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Food/ PRACTICES.

10. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. joule (J)
   B. pascal (Pa)
   C. newton (N)
   D. watt (W)

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Our ENVIRONMENT? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Our ENVIRONMENT.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Our ENVIRONMENT.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Our ENVIRONMENT.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Our ENVIRONMENT.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Neighbourhood ENVIRONMENT? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Neighbourhood ENVIRONMENT.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Neighbourhood ENVIRONMENT.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Neighbourhood ENVIRONMENT.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Neighbourhood ENVIRONMENT.

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying PRACTICES? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about PRACTICES.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to PRACTICES.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on PRACTICES.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for PRACTICES.

14. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Dressing ENVIRONMENT? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Dressing ENVIRONMENT.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Dressing ENVIRONMENT.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Dressing ENVIRONMENT.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Dressing ENVIRONMENT.

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Care PRACTICES? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Care PRACTICES.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Care PRACTICES.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Care PRACTICES.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Care PRACTICES.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Care PRACTICES and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Care for PRACTICES be able to; and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Toileting PRACTICES and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Food/ PRACTICES and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Plants ENVIRONMENT and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Animals ENVIRONMENT and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
